notes:
Account summary: Skyward CodeBench builds an IDE-focused copilot and low-latency code completion engine for enterprise dev teams. Highly sensitive to interactive latency during 'peak developer hours' (weekday mornings). They are evaluating Redwood Dedicated to guarantee predictable throughput with burst policies.

Recent timeline: 
- 2025-01-15: Intro call (AE Aisha) — product fit: ide copilot + team-level model pinning. Customer quote: "We need completions that feel instant for 400+ devs at once."
- 2025-01-23: Deep-dive with SE (Derek Wong) — walked through batching, kv cache, and streaming demo (Fireflies ff_20250123_8432).
- 2025-01-29: Security kickoff with InfoSec; asked for SOC2/ISO references and KMS integration (Fireflies ff_20250129_9121).
- 2025-01-31: Demo of streaming latency on hosted API against internal microbench — good functional match but noisy p95 under load.
- 2025-02-01: POC kickoff plan agreed: dedicated pool sized for 400 concurrent editors, simulate peak 9-11am PST, 2-week telemetry window, include sticky routing tests and per-workspace model pinning.

Requirements / asks (from product + infra):
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 80ms token-turnaround for streaming completions; p95 < 250ms under 95th percentile of simulated load.
- Throughput: sustain 6k requests/minute steady during peak, with ability to burst to 12k reqs/min for short spikes.
- Developer UX: low-chatter streaming (chunk sizes ~8-12 tokens), immediate partial suggestions, cancel/resume support.
- Model management: per-workspace version pinning, canary rollouts to 5% of org, automatic fallback to smaller quantized variant on overload.
- Cost sensitivity: moderate — prefer dedicated reserved capacity for predictability but want Optimize recommendations to reduce unit cost.
- Security & compliance: SSO/SAML mandatory, KMS for key controls, audit logs with 90-day retention, optional EU data residency for some customers.

POC notes / config items: 
- Sim plan: synthetic agents to mimic editor behavior (burstiness, short commands, multi-file requests).
- Runtime config: suggest dedicated pool with predictable slot units and a 20% burst buffer; enable prefix caching between sessions for repeated repo patterns.
- Metrics to capture: tokens/sec, token-latency distribution, request queue time, cost-per-1000-tokens.

Customer sentiment / quotes: 
- "If we lose the instantaneous feel, adoption drops — latency is king." — Head of Product (Skyward).
- Interested in per-route cost dashboards: "We need token-cost per workspace for chargeback."

Open items / blockers: 
- InfoSec to sign off on KMS integration and audit log retention (requested security FAQ in Drive).
- Procurement needs a 12-month predictable billing option for Dedicated; finance is evaluating ARR impact.
- On-prem latency tests scheduled (customer wants to simulate internal NAT and enterprise proxies).

Next actions (AE/SE): 
- 2025-02-03: Start dedicated POC provisioning (Aisha/Derek).
- 2025-02-05: Deliver scoped SOW draft + pricing band for 12-month reserved pool (Aisha).
- 2025-02-07: Run first peak-day sim and share telemetry dashboard (Derek).

Linked artifacts: drive docs (POC config + Security FAQ), Gmail threads for procurement, Fireflies recordings of technical calls.

Short-hand CRM notes: 
- prioritized: latency, pinned-versions, predictable costs
- decision-makers: Head of Product, VP Eng, InfoSec
- timeline: wants procurement decision by 2025-03

Stated risk: if p95 can't meet target during simulated peak, they will re-evaluate self-host + local inference (higher infra effort but control).
